title: Handmade gates craned into place at Rochdale Canal lock in Manchester

evidence_packet.title: Handmade gates craned into place at Rochdale Canal lock in Manchester
evidence_packet.lead: The new gates at Rochdale Canal lock in Manchester replace ones installed more than 25 years ago
evidence_packet.summary: The new gates at Rochdale Canal lock in Manchester replace ones installed more than 25 years ago
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Handmade gates craned into place at Rochdale Canal lock in Manchester - BBC News Image source, PA Image caption, The new gates have come from Yorkshire, replacing locks that were more than 25 years old By Georgie Docker North West Published 1 hour ago Work has begun to restore lock gates across Greater Manchester's historical canal network. A team has started fitting new handmade gates at Lock 80 on the Rochdale Canal, a waterway opened in 1804 as the first of three trans-Pennine canals, running between Manchester and Sowerby Bridge, West Yorkshire. The new gates, at the lock to the east of the city centre in Manchester, were handcrafted from oak in Yorkshire, before being craned into place. Each leaf of the upstream gate weighs one-and-a-half tonnes (1,500 kg), and the downstream leaves weigh two-and-a-half tonnes (2,500 kg). They replace gates that were installed at the turn of the millennium. It comes after canal gates were replaced in the stretch of canal running through Manchester's Gay Village, in February. Image source, PA Image caption, The new locks are critical to keeping canals open, the Canal and River Trust said The Canal and River Trust, the charity that cares for canals and waterways across England and Wales, said the work was one of hundreds of projects over the next five months set to maintain the 2,000-mile canal network. This year's programme will see the replacement of 136 lock gate leaves – the individual doors or panels – as well as repairs to historic locks, bridges, embankments and other infrastructure. Elsewhere in the North West, there will also be repairs to five locks on the Marple Flight on the Peak Forest Canal in Greater Manchester and two locks on the Wigan Flight of the Leeds and Liverpool Canal in Lancashire. Image source, PA Image capt

evidence_packet.summary: Daniel Rayner is one of nine men accused of sexual offences against a woman from Stockport

evidence_packet.summary: Drivers still face delays while a fuel spill is cleared while one anticlockwise lane remains shut
evidence_packet.evidence_text: The M60 remains partially closed after a lorry crashed through the central reservation barriers, causing a large fuel spill National Highways said the motorway was still shut clockwise between junction 13 for Worsley and junction 15 for the M61 while the fuel was cleared The anticlockwise M60 has partially reopened, but lane three remains closed between junctions 15 and 14 because of damage to the barriers Drivers are still facing delays of about 30 minutes in the area, National Highways said The crash happened at junction 15, where the M60 meets the M61 just before 07:30 GMT, National Highways said. It had followed an earlier crash in the same area National Highways said the lorry had crossed from the anticlockwise carriageway

title: Schools, libraries and parents face 'difficult decision' over David Walliams books

evidence_packet.title: Schools, libraries and parents face 'difficult decision' over David Walliams books
evidence_packet.lead: Some schools remove the children's author's books from their libraries after allegations against him
evidence_packet.summary: Some schools remove the children's author's books from their libraries after allegations against him
evidence_packet.evidence_text: "Head teachers are already making difficult decisions about whether or not these books should remain on the bookshelves of libraries at the moment," said Pepe Di'Iasio, general secretary of the Association of School and College Leaders "I'm aware from several of our members that they've already taken the decision to take them off their shelves." Walliams sold more than 50 million copies of books including Gangsta Granny and Billionaire Boy. He has denied allegations of sexual misconduct and abuses of power Darren Morgan, head of Kings Road Primary School in Manchester, told the programme that he has taken the decision to remove Walliams' publications The stories have been useful to promote reading, but "when there are these allegations it's really difficult to keep these books on the shelves", he said Steve Chalke, head of Oasis Academies, which runs more than 50 schools, said it was impossible to stop children seeing the current stories about Walliams

evidence_packet.summary: Manchester will receive cash from the government to help end rough sleeping by Christmas
evidence_packet.evidence_text: £846k fund to get people off Manchester's streets by Christmas - BBC News Image source, Reuters Image caption, Funding has been given to Manchester to get rough sleepers off the streets by Christmas By Marc Waddington North West Published 12 November 2026 Just under £850,000 has been given to Manchester to get people sleeping rough off the streets by Christmas. The money was handed down by the government, and comes after Prime Minister Andy Burnham pledged to end rough sleeping across the country. Manchester City Council plans to give the money to organisations that work with homeless people to help them find a "route off the streets". Figures published in March showed that the number of people sleeping rough in Manchester had increased on the previous 12 months. There were 59 people without a bed for the night, up from the previous year but lower than the March 2024 figure of 65. Tracey Rawlins, the deputy leader at Manchester City Council, welcomed the extra funding. She said: "The factors which lead to people living on the streets are complicated, so those routes cannot be 'one size fits all' and may include treatment for addiction or mental health issues and other intensive support, not only accommodation." "It's about putting the right values and the right standards at the heart of government." evidence_packet.title: Dad 'held falling lamp' during his wife's labour at Stepping Hill
evidence_packet.lead: Stepping Hill's boss says the hospital in Stockport needs "at least £400m" to tackle building issues
evidence_packet.summary: Stepping Hill's boss says the hospital in Stockport needs "at least £400m" to tackle building issues
evidence_packet.evidence_text: A new father said he had to hold up a light that had fallen from the maternity ward ceiling while his baby was being born below Jules Wilkinson said the lamp "started to unscrew itself" at Stepping Hill Hospital in Stockport while his wife was in labour The Greater Manchester hospital's chief executive said the site needed "at least £400m" to address building issues, while Cheadle MP Tom Morrison said he was raising the matter in Parliament The government said Stepping Hill was receiving tens of millions of pounds for maintenance and new buildings Wilkinson said as his wife was giving birth, the lamp almost hit the midwife "in the head" as it fell out of the ceiling Wilkinson told BBC North West Tonight he put the lamp on his shoulders "literally hanging on by the cord" and held on to it "for the next hour or so" until his baby had been delivered

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Manchester City Centre Huge 17-storey tower to loom over historic Marble Arch pub as plans recommended for approval The plans are among those set to be scrutinised at the next Manchester council planning committee meeting Add to preferred sources Comm Plans to build a 17-storey tower metres away from a historic Manchester pub are being recommended for approval despite fears the boozer may not survive the development process An apartment block with 153 flats is being planned for a plot next to the Grade II listed Marble Arch pub on Rochdale Road. The proposal is set to be reviewed at Manchester council's planning meeting on November 19, alongside plans to build two new student accommodation developme The plan on Rochdale Road was previously voted down by members of the planning committee on October 22. At the hearing, a representative from the Marble Arch said: “During construction, conditions inside and outside the pub are likely to be intolerable for customers “Marble Beers have genuine fear that their business will not survive the construction programme.” For developers McGoff Group, the application highlighted the benefits of new homes in the city centre, saying the application would ‘bring together the essential ingredients of successful regeneration.’

The work, to the east of the city centre on the historic Rochdale Canal, is part of the Canal and River Trust's extensive programme of winter repairs covering 2,00 Earlier this week, a team started fitting new lock gates at Lock 80, near Miles Platting and Victoria Mill. The waterway opened in 1804 as the first of three trans-Pennine canals, running between Manchester and Sowerby Bridge, West Yorkshire The charity, which cares for canals and waterways across England and Wales, said it would be carrying out hundreds of projects over the next five months to maintain the 'living heritage' of the network that was built in the industrial revolution and still functions today Around 136 lock gate leaves – the individual doors or panels – will be replaced under the national programme, as well as repairs to historic locks, bridges, embankments and other infrastructure The new lock gates in Manchester have been handcrafted from oak at the Canal and River Trust's lock gate workshop at Stanley Ferry, Yorkshire, before being craned into place

It’s only a 1.5-metre gap in a high brick wall all the wa But it’s one of the few legally accessible viewpoints left of the Winterbottom Reservoir since it was closed the public around nine years ago “It settles my mind coming here to look at the reservoir,” said the 37-year-old NHS worker. “I wish we could still get onto it, but I come and look through this crack in the fence and it gives me a sense of calm, watching the herons, the fish swimming about.” Much of the land is overgrown and peppered with fly-tipping. The by-election was called after the former leader of Oldham Reform Mark Wilkinson stood down as councillor citing health issues Reform and Labour have been campaigning hard in recent weeks, with some speculation the presence of Restore Britain in the race could hurt Reform’s chances. Failsworth West was won by Reform easily in May 2026 where they took 56 percent of the vote share compared to Labour’s 17pc As the results came in November 12, the by-election was much closer with Reform on 41.5pc compared to Labour’s 38.8pc, and Restore’s 11pc. However, Labour's 21pc surge was not enough to regain the seat The race was also a key test for Reform after two changes in leadership in recent months, resignations and suspensions, and criticism on social media from some supporters of the party. The scheme could see 434 new homes created, along with 172 hotel rooms There would also be ‘opportunities for cafés, shops and other uses that bring activity to the street, create more welcoming frontages, and encourage people to spend time in the area’. Add to preferred sources News Declan Carey Local Democracy Reporter 17:29, 12 Nov 2026 People living in Manchester's India House - which is covered in scaffolding - have been told their ‘nightmare’ will continue until 2028. The block, on Whitworth Street, is managed by the Guinne It has had scaffolding around the building on and off for the last six years, people living there say. The scaffolding first went up for works on the roof. Residents say it has made life ‘miserable’ First built between 1905 and 1912, India House was a packing warehouse before being converted into flats from 1988. Parts of it are Grade-II listed The building was one one of the first in Manchester city centre to provide social housing, and was home to Oasis star Noel Gallagher in the 1990s where he wrote songs for Oasis albums Definitely Maybe and What’s the Story, Morning Glory A meeting was called by Guinness at Friends Meeting House last week to give residents an update on the situation. One person said the gathering ‘descended into chaos’ and that people were left ‘more confused and upset’

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Fallowfield The moment brazen, smirking burglar was caught red-handed at 2am Fazal Alnensi, 26, has now been jailed Add to preferred sources Comments News John Scheerhout Crime reporter 18:46, 11 Nov 2026 View 3 Images Fazal Alnensi smirks as he's cau Police body cam footage captures the moment cops caught a brazen burglar red-handed at 2am. As cops arrived at the home in Fallowfield, a shocked householder told officers: "He's still in my house." When officers went into the property, they saw prolific burglar Fazal Alnensi, who sheepishly stood up from a chair he was sitting on and smiled as he coolly said 'hello' When he was pointed out as a thief, he was arrested on suspicion of burglary and led away. The 26-year-old has now been jailed. The householder returned to his home in Fallowfield at around 2.25am on June 12 this year, to find Alnensi inside Michael MartinThe burglar claimed he was only there because he wanted a glass of water but he refused to leave and officers who were called subsequently found a set of car keys belonging to the homeowner in his pockets Alnensi had been 'rummaging' through drawers in the property, according to Greater Manchester Police

Grealish has missed his side’s last four matches due to illness, a breach of club discipline and a lack of fitness However the on-loan Manchester City star returned to Finch Farm late last week to start a tailored training programme. And he stepped up his return to action on Thursday afternoon by playing the full 90 minutes in the 4-1 behind-closed-doors victory over Derby County And just hours after that game concluded at Hill Dickinson Stadium, Grealish took to Instagram to issue an apology to everyone connected to the club for not being available for selection over the last couple of weeks He wrote: "Nice to be back out there with the boys today after a few good days training! I want to apologise to the fans n everyone at the club for not been able to help the team the last few weeks, reports The Echo "I love playing for this club and I can't and I can't wait to be playing back infront of you guys in an Everton shirt. John Gizzi, known as Rhyl's 'Mr Big', told Natasha Farah, known as Tasha, to 'die and do us all a favour', rammed her car and threatened He also pushed her into a hotel swimming pool and tossed her clothes onto a roof when he found her at a train station. She was later found injured in April this year. She suffered brain damage and now needs round the clock hospital care At Mold Crown Court on Thursday, 55-year-old Gizzi was sentenced to four years in jail for coercive and controlling behaviour. He was also handed 11 more months behind bars for the intentional strangulation of her sister, Samantha There is no evidence Gizzi was directly responsible for the injuries Tasha sustained, but he was responsible for the "worst case" of domestic and psychological violence that a judge had ever seen, the court heard The Farah family branded Gizzi a "monster" and "the devil in disguise". Tasha's mum Denise Farah read a statement to the court detailing the "devastating impact” of Gizzi’s actions on the whole family, reports The Echo

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Oldham The £5m firm and the row over an Oldham mill its owners claim is 'eyesore' There are plans to convert the site into new homes but not everyone is happy about the idea Add to preferred sources Comments News Edward Barnes Local Democracy Reporter An international firm is in a dispute with its landlord over the use of an Oldham mill its owners claim is an ‘eyesore’. The disagreement came to light after plans for 26 homes were put forward for Wall Hill Mill, off Wall Hill Road in Dobcross The plans would see the buildings demolished. The Saddleworth site sits in the greenbelt, but is classed as previously developed land due to the presence of the mill. There is a large industrial building at the plot, as well as the remains of the older mill Homes in the area have previously been granted planning permission and the land’s owners argue assessments show the land is unviable for employment K&M Global Limited, the firm renting the site, opposes the changes. The company says it is thriving, employs 25 people, has a turnover in excess of £5m a year and invested £300,000 in improving the site The company is a vehicle dismantler, servicer and recycling business. It has been using the site for the last six years. Alan Chorlton , from Chorlton Planning and defending the firm, said it exports to Cyrpus and South Africa

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Manchester City Centre Huge new lock gates handcrafted from oak lowered into Rochdale Canal 'These repairs and renewals are critical to keeping canals open' Add to preferred sources Comments News Paul Britton Reporter 06:12, 13 Nov 2026 View 3 Images Huge new handcrafted lock gates are being lifted into place along a stretch of the canal in Manchester city centre . The work, to the east of the city centre on the historic Rochdale Canal, is part of the Canal and River Trust's extensive programme of winter repairs covering 2,00 Earlier this week, a team started fitting new lock gates at Lock 80, near Miles Platting and Victoria Mill. The waterway opened in 1804 as the first of three trans-Pennine canals, running between Manchester and Sowerby Bridge, West Yorkshire The charity, which cares for canals and waterways across England and Wales, said it would be carrying out hundreds of projects over the next five months to maintain the 'living heritage' of the network that was built in the industrial revolution and still functions today Around 136 lock gate leaves – the individual doors or panels – will be replaced under the national programme, as well as repairs to historic locks, bridges, embankments and other infrastructure The new lock gates in Manchester have been handcrafted from oak at the Canal and River Trust's lock gate workshop at Stanley Ferry, Yorkshire, before being craned into place

The block, on Whitworth Street, is managed by the Guinne It has had scaffolding around the building on and off for the last six years, people living there say. The scaffolding first went up for works on the roof. Residents say it has made life ‘miserable’ First built between 1905 and 1912, India House was a packing warehouse before being converted into flats from 1988. Schedule 1 includes smaller and more technical applications that would only be dealt with by planning officers Schedule 2 covers larger applications, which may be brought before the planning committee, if agreed by the planning committee chair and the council’s chief planning officer. The move also removes elected members’ right to ‘call in’ a planning application for scrutiny and debate The new rules came into force at the end of October, with Bury council now having approved the change in its constitution needed to meet the new legal requirements. The motion was passed by the Labour group, which holds a majority on the authority. All opposition councillors vote

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Bury ‘Serious safety failings’ found in Bury council social housing inspection, watchdog warns The council could not show it was meeting the ‘legally required timescales’ to investigate, identify and repair hazards such as damp and mould, while 2,800 Outcomes in safety and accountability were judged to be particularly poor, with the Regulator of Social Housing saying it cannot be sure the town hall is meeting its legal duties. The town hall owns around 7,600 homes with some 300 of these managed by an external agency It was the council’s first inspection under the regulatory framework and it was awarded a C3 rating – the second lowest outcome. The council took its housing services back into direct management in 2024 as it began to wind down social housing provider Six Town Housing (STH) It is in the process of consulting on the future of the remaining around 100 homes managed by STH, with a recent report recommending that these too be brought under the council control. The council believes that will offer ‘greater long-term stability’ for tenants, with alternati Among the concerns raised by inspectors were overdue fire safety remedial actions, with 2,800 outstanding at the time of the inspection. While most were assessed as being low to medium risk, the Regulator of Social Housing said there was a ‘lack of clarity’ about the time taken t The council also could not show it was meeting the ‘legally required timescales’ to investigate, identify and repair hazards such as damp and mould

Credit: Canal & River Trust / Spectrum Freight Ltd / Ote Lifting Ltd /Press Association Work is taking place to fit new lock gates in Manchester ’s historic Rochdale Can The Canal and River Trust, the charity that cares for canals and waterways across England and Wales , said it would be carrying out hundreds of projects over the next five months to maintain the “living heritage” of the network that was built in the industrial revolution and stil This year’s programme will see the replacement of lock gate leaves, the individual doors or panels as well as repairs to historic locks, bridges, embankments and other infrastructure Earlier this week, a team started fitting new lock gates at Lock 80 on the Rochdale Canal, a waterway opened in 1804 as the first of three trans-Pennine canals, running between Manchester and Sowerby Bridge, West Yorkshire The new gates, at the lock to the east of the city centre in Manchester, have been handcrafted from oak at the Canal and River Trust’s lock gate workshop at Stanley Ferry, Yorkshire, before being craned into place T he charity saidEach leaf of the upstream gate weighs 1.5 tonnes, and the downstream leaves weigh 2.5 tonnes, and replace gates that were installed around the turn of the millennium

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Michael Martin, from Salford, was reported missing on 8 August 2016 after the then 25-year-old was last seen at a petrol station on Bolton Road , in Kearsley, Bolton, the day before Ten years on, detectives investigating his murder have offered the reward to try find his body His father, Gregg Martin, said the "not-knowing is gut wrenching every day" and added: "We know he's dead but it's just not knowing where he was, where he is and what happened to him. It'd give the family some closure – a form of sort of peace." He added: "My message to the people is to do the right thing – tell someone or indirectly let the police know what happened to Michael so we can get some peace of mind and closure." Greater Manchester Police has treated the investigation as a "non-body murder" since 2016 The renewed appeal for information leading to Martin's body comes after, in 2018, police offered £50,000 for information on Martin's disappearance

title: Portland Street to reopen as emergency repairs come to a conclusion

evidence_packet.lead: Manchester City Council can announce that Portland Street will be reopened to traffic from the early hours of Wednesday morning (November 4)
evidence_packet.summary: Manchester City Council can announce that Portland Street will be reopened to traffic from the early hours of Wednesday morning (November 4)
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Manchester City Council can announce that Portland Street will be reopened to traffic from the early hours of Wednesday morning (November 4) This follows an extensive programme of emergency repairs due to a broken water main which ruptured last week A large-scale operation was put into action to isolate the source of the leak and repair it, and then carry out a full repair and resurface of the damaged road Crews from United Utilities and the Council have worked around the clock since Friday afternoon to ensure that the road could be reopened as quickly and safely as possible. This has been alongside TfGM staff who have also put additional resource into redirecting affected public t Illustrating the scale of the repairs needed, roughly 600 tonnes of road surface has been planed away and replaced over the course of these works The restrictions on the road are planned to be removed early on Wednesday morning (November 4), with the road practicably useable to motorists shortly after that

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Residents in Saddleworth will have the opportunity to vote on the future of planning in their area when a referendum takes place on Thursday 10 December 2026. The referendum will ask residents whether they want Oldham Council and the Peak District National Park Authority to use the Saddleworth Neighbourhood Plan to help decide planning applications in the area. The plan sets out local planning policies for Saddleworth and, if approved, will become part of the area’s statutory Development Plan, helping to guide decisions on future planning applications. Residents will be asked the following question: “Do you want Oldham Council and the Peak District National Park Authority to use the Neighbourhood Plan for Saddleworth to help it decide planning applications in the neighbourhood area?” To vote, residents must be registered to vote in local government elections and have a qualifying address within the Saddleworth Neighbourhood Area. The deadline to register to vote is Tuesday 24 November 2026. Residents who wish to vote by post, proxy or who need a Voter Authority Certificate should also be aware of the following deadlines: - Wednesday 25 November, 5pm: Deadline for new postal vote applications and changes to existing postal voting arrangements. - Wednesday 2 December, 5pm: Deadline for new proxy vote applications and applications for a free Voter Authority Certificate. - Thursday 10 December, 5pm: Deadline for emergency proxy vote applications, where eligible. Residents can read the Saddleworth Neighbourhood Plan and supporting referendum documents online at: https://www.oldham.gov.uk/info/201235/neighbourhood_planning/2936/saddleworth_neighbourhood_plan Paper copies are also available to view at Lees, Uppermill, Delph and Greenfield libraries, Oldham Council’s reception

While the New Year deadline feels quite a distance away to some, data held by Rochdale Borough Council shows families still miss this important deadline. In 2026, 216 parents submitted a late primary school application. This led to more than a third of those children (37%) missing out on their first preferred school as a result when reception started this September. In comparison, 89% of those who submitted an application on time secured their preferred school. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Experience the raw, unfiltered power of Balkan folklore in a new immersive show from the world’s most famous performance artist Balkan Erotic Epic is a bold new performance work created by the iconic artist Marina Abramović . Regarded as the world’s most influential performance artist, Abramović’s transformative work has reached millions of people – from opening the Pyramid Stage at Glastonbury Festival t A four-hour ritual where ancient myth meets performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic explores the eroticism, spirituality and traditions of Abramović’s homeland through 13 visceral scenes Brought to life by a cast of over 70 performers, dancers, musicians and singers, the experience unfolds across Aviva Studios. Audiences are free to choose their own path – with pop-up encounters punctuating the action, bringing bodies together in dance, song and ritual Watch Fertility Rite , a fevered ritual where bodies writhe against the ground in a desperate call for fertility. Witness Massaging the Breast where women gesticulate over graves to awaken the earth. In Scaring the Gods , women bare themselves to the sky to banish storms. Listen Unafraid to push the boundaries of eroticism and performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic asks its audience a timeless question: What are our bodies truly for?

Everyone visiting the store will receive a scratch card, with prizes ranging from discounts on purchases to Saucony giveaways, including free trainers On Saturday 14 November, the focus shifts from collecting trainers to actually putting them through their paces. Saucony is teaming up with Ancoats-based running club Laterunnrers for a relaxed 5K community run, setting off from the pop-up at 10am. Everyone’s welcome, regardless The pop-up is open Friday from 10am to 4pm, Saturday from 10am to 6pm and Sunday from 11am to 4pm. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Sun 15th Nov, 2026 - Locations across Stockport town centre ©Matthew Nichol Photography Stockport’s Spectacular Sunday Locations across Stockport town centre Sun 15th Nov, 2026 12pm - 5pm Go to Manchester's Finest X profile A giant snow lion, a circus adventure into space and the world’s smallest nightclub. Stockport is kicking off Christmas in suitably weird and wonderful fashion, as Spectacular Sunday returns for its fourth year on Sunday 15 November More than 200 performers and 50 free shows will take over the town centre, transforming streets and squares into stages for giant puppets, circus acts, live music, comedy and all manner of festive surprises Among the highlights is the enormous Snow Lion, joined by dancing elves and towering stiltwalkers. There’s also Over The Moon, a circus adventure with an intergalactic twist, and Hydropunk, an interactive spectacle involving water-powered pipes, pumps, sprays and puzzles And if you fancy a rave between the Christmas shopping, The Miniscule of Sound, officially the world’s smallest nightclub, is back for another year. Expect big tunes in a very, very small space

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Get ready for a huge dose of boy band nostalgia as Boys Are Back Again hits venues across the UK Headlining the tour are the legendary East 17, one of the UK’s biggest ever boy bands and true trailblazers of the 90s pop era. The show blends Mandé griot tradition with blues, Afropop and contemporary songwriting. She has also toured with blues legend Taj Mahal. Her concerts have become events wherever she plays. She has performed more than a hundred shows across Europe, Africa, the United States and beyond, in some of the world’s most prestigious theaters and festivals, with sell-outs at London’s Barbican, Cologne’s Philharmonie and the Seine Musicale in Paris, and appearances at the Hollywood Bowl, Symphony Space in New York and WOMAD Australia and New Zealand. Her latest album, Badinyaa Kumoo, was named one of the best albums of its year by Songlines Magazine, and her single “Gambia” has passed 32 million YouTube views. Recent collaborations include a feature on LL Cool J’s album The FORCE, on the song “Black Code Suite”, and a guest appearance on “Se a Vida Pede” from the Brazilian group Gilsons’ latest album. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Finish work and unwind with live music from Manchester’s best jazz musicians. Beat the Jams live series showcases the very best of the jazz scene, at short rush hour gigs from 6pm at Band on the Wall. What better way to avoid those endless queues, chaotic traffic and stressful homeward journeys? Clock off and skip the rush-hour traffic while you watch live jazz and make the most of our happy hour deals from 5–7pm: £4.50 pints / 2 for £15 cocktails / £15 bottles of wine + pizzas from £5! The new season kicks off on 24 September with tenor saxophonist Dean Masser and pianist Richard Wetherall, followed by: 7 October – Anna Chandler-King Quartet Leeds based saxophonist and composer Anna joins us again for Beat the Jams, this time with her own band. Anna’s thoughtful and inventive compositions are firm favourites of us at Beat the Jams and her quartet promises to be a unique rush hour busting treat! 16 November – Sam Lightwing Quartet Saxophonist and composer Sam Lightwing brings presents brand new music for his thrilling young quartet, showcasing Sam’s original compositions, which blend classic mainstream jazz grooves with modern flavours of post-pop and latin, all wrapped up in the language of contemporary sax giants such as Chris Potter, Seamus Blake and Joshua Redman. 15 December – Svarc/Devine/Walsh with Richard Iles The band combines deep pocket, fearless interplay and a shared love of exploration. Expect everything from soulful melodies and infectious rhythms to moments of exhilarating collective improvisation, delivered with the chemistry that only world-class musicians can create. Retirement was being seriously considered. Instead, Roger decided to “go again properly” That decision has resulted in a new long-term commitment to the Chop Houses and around £300,000 being spent restoring Tom’s – touching everything from the dining rooms and furniture to the menu, wine list, kitchen and beer cellars Roger is particularly pleased with the toilets “Tom’s was famous for the shittest toilets in town,” he says. It is Open Restaurant Group’s ninth restaurant to date and its second site in Greater Manchester, following the launch of Arcadian in Didsbury in Sep At the focus of the restaurant is a four-to-five-seat chef’s counter, which places guests directly at the pass for an up-close view of the kitchen in action. The interiors feature four-metre elm trees, curved booth seating and a brass wine display, so the atmosphere and experienc Award-winning Andrew Sheridan brings his internationally inspired approach to Counter, building on a career that has seen multiple restaurants under his direction feature in the prestigious Michelin Guide. At Counter, he challenges convention by exploring what British cooking can The menu puts this philosophy into practice with dishes that combine unexpected ingredients and inventive flavour pairings. Highlights include the Beef Tartare Pressed Croissant, pairing aged beef with a crispy pressed croissant, smoked oyster mayo, wasabi and pickled shallot and From the grill, guests can enjoy the Satay Spatchcock Chicken, served with peanut satay, fermented chilli, coconut, burnt lime and crispy shallot, alongside the slow-cooked Thai Lamb Shoulder, served with red thai sauce, chilli and coriander

evidence_packet.lead: The government's new Digital and Technologies Jobs Plan aims to create 200,000 entry-level jobs over the next decade, recognising the barriers facing employers and the importance of regional organisations in connecting people with opportunities.
evidence_packet.summary: The government's new Digital and Technologies Jobs Plan aims to create 200,000 entry-level jobs over the next decade, recognising the barriers facing employers and the importance of regional organisations in connecting people with opportunities. The government has published its D
evidence_packet.evidence_text: The government's new Digital and Technologies Jobs Plan aims to create 200,000 entry-level jobs over the next decade, recognising the barriers facing employers and the importance of regional organisations in connecting people with opportunities. The government has published its D The plan acknowledges that the challenge is not simply a shortage of people with digital skills. Entry-level recruitment has become more difficult, with employers increasingly favouring experienced candidates and many graduates and other new entrants struggling to secure their fi Manchester Digital contributed to the development of the plan through its involvement in the government's Digital Skills Council, drawing on its work with employers and education providers across Greater Manchester Around 800,000 digital and technology roles are projected to need filling over the next decade. The plan sets out an ambition to create 200,000 entry-level jobs, including apprenticeships, during that period The plan also addresses how AI is changing workforce requirements and the importance of ensuring people entering the industry have both technical knowledge and practical workplace skills Manchester Digital's 2026 Sector Insights Report highlighted a reduction of around 20% in early-career opportunities, despite continued demand for experienced technology professionals

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Bolton Car Boot Sale is one of the North West's biggest weekly boot sales, held in the hardstanding car park of the Macron Stadium (formerly Reebok), Burnden Way, Horwich, Bolton BL6 6JW. It runs every Sunday from February right through to December, drawing over 300 sellers and thousands of bargain hunters each week. Sellers can arrive and set up from 6:00 AM, with buyers welcomed in from 7:00 AM. Entry costs just £1 per car for buyers. Pitches for sellers are £14 for a car, £20 for a van and £3 for a trailer, with regular and corner pitches available on request. Bring exact change to keep the queue moving, and call organiser Andrew on 07470784644 for more details. Expect hundreds of stalls across the concrete hardstanding pitches, so it goes ahead in most weather. On-site you'll find a 5-star catering service, doughnuts and coffee, ice cream and desserts, a meat auction, fresh fruit and veg, plants, and retro sweet stalls. The sale is dog-friendly, has male and female toilets, ample parking, and kids' rides and bouncy castles to keep little ones entertained. title: One obvious Mauricio Pochettino question remains as he fulfils his destiny at Manchester United

evidence_packet.title: One obvious Mauricio Pochettino question remains as he fulfils his destiny at Manchester United
evidence_packet.lead: Mauricio Pochettino has long seemed destined to take charge of Man Utd and he is finally about to see that turn into reality
evidence_packet.summary: Mauricio Pochettino has long seemed destined to take charge of Man Utd and he is finally about to see that turn into reality
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Football Manchester United FC One obvious Mauricio Pochettino question remains as he fulfils his destiny at Manchester United Mauricio Pochettino has long seemed destined to take charge of Man Utd and he is finally about to see that turn into reality. Add to preferred sourc It can be easy to accuse Manchester United of living in the past, but sometimes the most obvious criticisms are also the most accurate ones. As their search for a new head coach comes to an end, club chiefs have turned to someone they rejected in 2019 and 2022 It's a parable of the modern-day Manchester United . They might not be going for a club legend now, but they are going for a head coach they should have appointed earlier, only to pass over him twice when his stock was higher than it is now Going for Mauricio Pochettino looks like the right call this time. He is the best of the available candidates, but that says more about the people he has beaten to the job than it does about the 54-year-old Argentine When your other alternatives were someone burnt out by an up-and-down spell at Newcastle and a head coach who failed with Bayern Munich and Germany, you don't really have to stand out to convince Omar Berrada and Jason Wilcox that you might just be the right man this time Get the best United news, updates and analysis straight to your Inbox courtesy of the Manchester Evening News!

Add to preferred sources Comments Sport opinion Steven R Even when Michael Carrick knew his time in charge of Manchester United was ending, he conducted himself with class Last month, Carrick defended Leny Yoro after his mistake against Bournemouth and responded in a political way when asked whether he agreed that United's board needed to take responsibility for their failings United fans have been desperate for Carrick to rip into Jason Wilcox and Omar Berrada, but he hasn't dragged himself into a public episode because of his deep respect for the club as an institution Get the best United news, updates and analysis straight to your Inbox courtesy of the Manchester Evening News!
